name: freelance-finance-tracker
summary: A privacy‑first freelance finance tracker built with Expo (React Native) and React Native Paper. All data (receipts, mileage logs, settings) is stored encrypted on the device using expo‑secure‑store for the key and @noble ciphers/hashes for encryption. The app requires a policy agreement on first launch (or when the policy version changes), supports receipt capture, mileage logging, a dashboard with income/expense/mileage‑deduction/tax calculations, CSV & PDF export, encrypted backup/restore with a user‑chosen passphrase, optional biometric lock, and a polished UI with shared components, theming, and a bottom tab bar. No network requests, analytics, or external services are used.
steps: Initialize a new Expo managed project with the TypeScript template (`expo init freelance-finance-tracker --template expo-template-blank-typescript`).

Install required dependencies: `expo-secure-store expo-sqlite expo-file-system expo-image-picker expo-local-authentication expo-sharing expo-print react-native-paper @react-navigation/native @react-navigation/native-stack @react-navigation/bottom-tabs @react-native-async-storage/async-storage @noble/ciphers @noble/hashes zustand`. Install dev dependencies for testing: `jest @testing-library/react-native @testing-library/jest-native @types/jest ts-jest`.
Configure `app.json` (or `app.config.ts`) to disable telemetry, analytics and expo-updates. Set `privacy` flag to `public` and ensure no remote endpoints are defined.
Create a Material 3 theme in `src/theme.ts` using React Native Paper's `MD3LightTheme`, customize colors and spacing, and export it for the app.

Build reusable UI components in `src/components/ui/`: `Screen` (wrapper with safe area and theming), `FormField` (label + TextInput), `PrimaryButton` (styled Paper button), `SummaryCard` (shows a numeric metric with icon), `EmptyState` (friendly placeholder), and `BottomTabNavigator` (bottom tab bar with icons for Dashboard, Receipts, Mileage, Settings).
Set up navigation in `src/navigation/index.tsx`: a Bottom Tab Navigator for the main sections and a Stack Navigator that places the `PolicyScreen` at the root when the policy is not accepted.
Implement policy agreement logic:
• Define a constant `POLICY_VERSION = "1.0"` (increment when the text changes).
• In `src/lib/policy.ts` write `getPolicyAcceptance(): Promise<{version: string, date: string}|null>` and `setPolicyAcceptance(version:string, date:string): Promise<void>` using `expo-secure-store`.
• Create `src/screens/PolicyScreen.tsx` that displays Terms of Use and Privacy Policy text, an “I Agree” checkbox, and a button that stores the current version and ISO date via `setPolicyAcceptance`.
• Add a `usePolicy` hook in `src/hooks/usePolicy.ts` that checks acceptance on app start and navigates to the Policy screen if missing or outdated.
Create an encrypted storage layer:

• In `src/lib/encryption.ts` implement `deriveKey(passphrase:string, salt:Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array>` using PBKDF2 (from `@noble/hashes`). Implement `encrypt(plaintext:Uint8Array, key:Uint8Array): Promise<{ciphertext:Uint8Array, iv:Uint8Array, tag:Uint8Array}>` and `decrypt(...)` using AES‑GCM from `@noble/ciphers`.

• In `src/lib/storage.ts` wrap `expo-sqlite` to open a SQLite DB located in the app's private file system. On each query, encrypt/decrypt column values with the key retrieved from `expo-secure-store` (key generated once on first launch and stored securely). Provide generic `run`, `get`, `all` helpers that hide encryption.

Define data models and CRUD helpers in `src/lib/records.ts`: TypeScript interfaces `Receipt`, `MileageEntry`, `Config`; functions `addReceipt`, `listReceipts`, `deleteReceipt`, `addMileage`, `listMileage`, `setConfig`, `getConfig` using the storage helpers.

Implement receipt capture in `src/screens/ReceiptsScreen.tsx`: use `expo-image-picker` to launch camera (fallback to library), store the resulting image in a private directory via `expo-file-system`, collect amount, date, category, type (expense/income), notes with `FormField` components, and persist with `addReceipt`.
Implement mileage entry in `src/screens/MileageScreen.tsx`: simple form for date, miles, purpose; on submit call `addMileage`.
Create calculation utilities in `src/lib/calculations.ts`:
• `getTotalIncome(): Promise<number>` – sum of receipt amounts where type is income.
• `getTotalExpenses(): Promise<number>` – sum of receipt amounts where type is expense.
• `getMileageDeduction(rate:number): Promise<number>` – total miles * rate.
• `getEstimatedTax(taxRate:number, income:number, expenses:number, mileageDeduction:number): number` – compute `(income - expenses - mileageDeduction) * taxRate` and clamp to >= 0.
Export a `useDashboardStats` hook that aggregates the above values and returns them for the Dashboard UI.

Build the Dashboard UI in `src/screens/DashboardScreen.tsx`: use `SummaryCard` components for Income, Expenses, Mileage Deduction, Estimated Tax; list recent activity (last 5 receipts/mileage entries) with icons; provide quick‑action buttons for “Add Receipt”, “Add Mileage”, “Export CSV”, “Export PDF”, and “Backup”.
Implement CSV export in `src/lib/backup.ts`:
• `exportCSV(): Promise<Uri>` creates a CSV string from receipts and mileage entries, writes it to a temporary `.csv` file using `expo-file-system`, and returns the file URI.
Implement PDF export using `expo-print` in `src/lib/backup.ts`:
• `exportPDF(): Promise<Uri>` builds a simple HTML template with tables of data, calls `Print.printToFileAsync`, and returns the generated PDF URI.
Implement encrypted backup & restore in `src/lib/backup.ts`:

• `createBackup(passphrase:string): Promise<Uri>` serializes the SQLite DB (e.g., `SELECT * FROM sqlite_master;` + data), bundles receipt image files (read via `expo-file-system`), creates a JSON or binary blob, encrypts it with a key derived from the passphrase, writes a `.backup` file in the app's file system, and returns its URI.

• `restoreBackup(passphrase:string, backupUri:string): Promise<void>` reads the backup file, decrypts using the derived key, verifies HMAC/integrity, rewrites the SQLite DB, restores images, and clears any in‑memory caches.
Add optional biometric lock:

• In `src/lib/auth.ts` implement `requireAuthIfEnabled(): Promise<boolean>` that reads a `lockEnabled` flag from Config, and if true calls `LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync` with appropriate prompt. Return true if authentication succeeds.
• Settings UI toggles the flag and persists it with `setConfig`.
Develop Settings screen in `src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx` with sections to:
• Toggle app lock, configure mileage rate (default IRS rate), configure tax rate (ensure non‑negative).
• View the current policy (navigate to `PolicyScreen`).
• Trigger backup (prompt for passphrase, call `createBackup`).
• Trigger restore (pick a `.backup` file via file picker, prompt for passphrase, call `restoreBackup`).
• Delete all data – show a confirmation alert, then clear SQLite DB, delete stored images, and remove the encryption key from SecureStore.
Write unit tests for core logic (policy acceptance, encryption round‑trip, calculations, backup creation/restoration, storage CRUD) in `__tests__/unit/` (the test runner will create these files).

Write integration tests for UI flow using `@testing-library/react-native` (policy gate, receipt addition, mileage addition, dashboard totals, backup UI) in `__tests__/integration/` (the test runner will generate them).
Configure Jest:
• Add a `jest.config.js` that uses `ts-jest`, sets the test environment to `node`, and maps module names for Expo APIs to mock implementations.

• Provide manual mocks for `expo-secure-store`, `expo-sqlite`, `expo-file-system`, `expo-image-picker`, `expo-local-authentication`, `expo-sharing`, `expo-print` that simulate their APIs in pure JavaScript.
Ensure the code respects the privacy‑first principle:
• No network fetches, no analytics packages, no error‑reporting SDKs.
• All secrets (encryption key) are only stored in SecureStore and never logged.
• All file paths are resolved within the app's private directory; no path concatenation with user input.
Finalize the project:
• Add a `README.md` with a clear privacy statement, usage guide, backup/restore instructions, and a note that the app never transmits data.
• Run `npm run lint` and `npm test` to ensure all acceptance tests pass.
• Build the production bundle with `expo export` (or `eas build` if using EAS) and verify that the bundle contains no external network calls.
